utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber apologises for the late start. Mr. Josse, we understood Mr. Krajisnik would like to address us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Does Your Honour wants the case called?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course. It's good, Mr. Josse, that you're there because otherwise things really go wrong. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That puts a smile on my face. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, this is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I hope, Mr. Josse, that I'll be able to make you forget that it's Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The message was almost correct. It's an instruction to me to put to the Court, Mr. Krajisnik would ask -- like me to ask the witness another few questions. I can tell the Court what the topic is. It's not in the 65 ter and it relates to imprisonment and then the subsequent departure of -- or the detention, perhaps I should say, and then the subsequent departure of Muslims from Pale. I'd ask the witness his knowledge as far as that is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, whilst we have no objection to Mr. Josse proceeding in regard to that topic, it may require us some time to consider the evidence that's given in light of it not being in the 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under those circumstances, we'll allow you, Mr. Josse, to put a few additional questions. At the same time, I really hope that this would not cause us to keep the witness for another day. That's -- but at the same time, let's see what happens. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Lakic into the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lakic. Please be seated. I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony, and I want to inform you that where you expected now to be cross-examined, there will be a few more questions put to you by Mr. Josse, counsel for the Defence, and we'll then continue with your cross-examination. Mr. Josse please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic in April and May of 1992, are you aware what happened to the Muslim population of Pale?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was by sheer coincidence that as I was on my way to work, saw a bus holding Muslims ready to leave. The situation was quite evident because both those who were on the bus leaving and those who were seeing them off were crying and those people who were seeing their lot off gave them flowers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Do you know when this was?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not really sure. Most probably it was the month of April, perhaps the month of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: So it follows from your answer that those who were leaving were of Muslim ethnicity. What about those who were seeing them off and giving them flowers? What ethnicity were those people?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Prior to the departure of the Pale Muslims, have you any idea where they were living?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: What was the hotel Koran used as or for?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a period of time, it was used to put up refugees and for a certain period of time it housed people who came to Pale to work there for a fixed period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of Muslims being detained anywhere in Pale?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That's all I want to ask. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Josse. Mr. Margetts, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lakic.

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, on Friday, at page 43 of the transcript, lines 21 to 24, you were asked the following question and you gave the following answer. And the question was, "What would have been the effect on the government and administration of Republika Srpska had a state of war been declared?" You answered, "By having declared a state of war, only the expanded presidency would have remained. Everything else would not, could not function." And earlier on the same page, page 43, that is, at lines 14 to 15, in the course of answering a question to why a state of war was not declared, you stated, "Once a state of war is declared, the functioning of all institutions in the RS are being put out of force, starting with the assembly and the government, down to the municipalities." Mr. Lakic, I'd like to hand you a document, and that is Article 9 of the Defence Act.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, the Defence Act has been previously exhibited as P65 tab 145. Unfortunately I reconciled the ERNs, identification numbers, this morning and found that the copy I have is a different ERN number. Furthermore the document that I'm distributing at the moment is an extract from the Defence Act, the first three pages, and so if we could have a new exhibit number for this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1109, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, if I could refer you in a B/C/S copy, this is the Official Gazette of Republika Srpska published on the 1st of June 1992, and if I could refer to you the second page of the document that you have, if you could open it and if you could look to the right-hand column you'll see Article 9 set out there, and Article 9 states as follows: "In case of a state of emergency, war or the imminent threat of war, ministries shall within their scope of activity, implement laws and war regulations, carry out the tasks set out in the defence plan of the republic, and be responsible for ensuring that the fields for which they have been established function properly." Mr. Lakic, Article 9 correctly sets out the role and function of the government in conditions of state of emergency, war or imminent threat of war, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand this latter question of yours. Can you tell me again which Article that is?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: On the second page, you'll see -- the first full article which is set out in the right-hand column is Article 9 and it consists of two paragraphs and the paragraph I read into the record is the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And my question was this: That first paragraph of Article 9 correctly sets out the role and the function of government in conditions of an imminent threat of war or a state of war, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I believe one ought to draw a distinction between the war, imminent threat of war, and declaring a state of war. The conditions underlying these are quite different from each other. When a state of war is declared, military regulations come into force, whereas all the civilian regulations become inapplicable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you, Mr. Lakic. Mr. Margetts is not asking about the different consequences but he points at Article 9 and there your earlier testimony was that by declaring a state of war, that only the expanded Presidency would have remained and that once a state of war is declared, the functioning of all institutions are being put out of force, he says, " Article 9 I read that even in a state of war, that still ministries would have their tasks even if adapted to the situation," but they would still have tasks. That's the question. Where you said that everything would be out of function, apart from the -- apart from the expanded Presidency.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One ought to distinguish the three expressions. Imminent threat of war, war, and a declaration of a state of war. The declaration of a state of war is something which makes all the civilian regulations inapplicable, when military regulations come into force, any relations with other countries are severed, and basically the state becomes isolated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, I have reviewed the constitution of Republika Srpska, the law on government, and the Defence Act. All of those provisions, all of the provisions in that legislation, state that the consequences of an imminent threat of war and the state of war are the same. Have I missed a provision? And if so, are you able to tell the Court what Article or what provision that is?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The constitution is the highest piece of legislation in the Republika Srpska, and all the secondary legislation is subordinated and subject to the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, are you able to tell the Court or inform the Court of a provision that supports your view that there is a distinction between the consequences of the declaration of imminent threat of war or a state of war?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Friday, I stated that there is such thing as an imminent threat of war, a state of war, and -- or, rather, a war, and lastly that there is such thing as a declaration of a state of war. One ought to distinguish among these three notions. As far as laws are concerned, they have to be harmonised with the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, I'd like to show you a further document and if I could refer to tab 9 in the materials that have been distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is an operative programme. We've seen this document before but not this specific copy of the document. So we will need a new exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1110, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, if you could turn to the cover page of this document, there is a letter that was written by you. It's written to the Ministry of Justice. It's dated 17 July 1992. It states, "Attached please find the operative programme of measures to prevent social disruption in conditions of a state of war." Do you recall writing that letter?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And if you look at the document that is attached, that is the operative programme referred to in the letter. Do you recognise that operative programme? Mr. Lakic, there is no need for you to read through the entire thing. I just want you to say whether or not you recognise that document.

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't draft this document. It was probably the Ministry of Defence who authored the document. I have to say that when a state of war is declared one must necessarily continue living and working in a given territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And this document was drafted so that the government could continue to function in a state of war, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that's the purpose of this document, but rather to create the basic conditions for the population to continue living in the territory of the Republika Srpska in the event of a war being declared, rather than to enable the authorities to function.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The steps set out in this operative programme were implemented, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The state of war was declared - I can't remember really - perhaps in mid-1995 or in late 1995, when the war was in its last stages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, Mr. Margetts asked you whether the steps set out in this programme were implemented. He did not ask when the state of war a was declared. He asked whether this programme was implemented which dates the 17th of July 1992. Could you please answer that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honours, if these interruptions are unhelpful -- I don't know what Your Honour will say but my learned friend specifically told the witness not to read the document. Realistically, can he answer that question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we have now two problems. First of all, the witness is not expected to answer a different question but if he can't answer that question, of course, he should say give me time to read it. But it makes some sense, Mr. Margetts. What you perhaps could do is just to summarise and say or give a few examples of the matters in this rather lengthy document. Mr. Lakic, apart from -- are you aware from memory approximately of what this document of the 17th of July contains?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Margetts, then you'll have to take the witness or summarise it in such a way that could -- would not be objected to by Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll proceed to do that but first if we could refer to a third document, which is tab 10, which is Exhibit P979.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, if you could have a look at the document which is P979 and which is at tab 10, and you will see that that document is a document emanating from the Presidency of Republika Srpska, and it's headed, "Guidelines on tasks, modes of action, and functioning of Defence forces, state organs and subjects in the field of economy and social activities in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the state of war." Now, this is a document that the Presidency prepared and forwarded to the government, and it refers to each of the ministries and sets out the tasks that they are to perform in the state of war. Have you seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I could refer you back to tab 9, which is the operative programme that you enclosed under cover of letter signed by you of 17 July 1992, and I could refer you to the first paragraph of the operative programme that you enclosed with that letter, so if you turn over the page, not the letter, if you look past the could have been page of the operative programme and at the first paragraph of the operative programme, that's correct, the paragraph at the top of that page, the page that's in front of you, it reads as follows: "Pursuant to Article 8 of the law on detention and with reference to the guidelines on the tasks and methods of action and functioning of Defence forces, state authorities, and entities in the economy and public services of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in conditions of a state of war, the government adopts this operative programme." Mr. Lakic, does that refresh your memory and do you see that this operative programme that you circulated was implementing the guidelines that I have just shown you?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the earlier testimony, I stated that I was a professional civil servant who did not go into the substance of the material. Each ministry provided its own comments, if any, which were then examined at a government meeting and integrated into the programme. My job was a technical one. I did not read the programme. It wasn't within my duties to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: So is your answer to my question, Mr. Lakic, that having read that first paragraph, it has refreshed your memory and you now do recall the guidelines from the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And following up on the previous answer that you gave, you do remember that this operative programme was referred to on numerous occasions in the government sessions, and you do recall that it was implemented, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think this programme was frequently discussed at government sessions. Every ministry was charged with implementing the programme, if applicable, and, of course, within the remit of its responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, my reading of the government minutes suggests that the programme was referred to on at least three occasions in the government sessions, they are the sessions of 8 July 1992, 16 July 1992, and 29 July 1992. Do you have any reason to dispute that it was referred to on those three occasions?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It's not a reasonable question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't concur with my learned friend but I'm willing to move on in the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because otherwise, at least, you should point at the sessions where it was referred to. You can refer to a programme as being rejected or you can refer to -- there are many possibilities, and put in this way it's better that you move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I could now refer to tab 48, and that's a letter from Mr. Lakic dated the 16th of August 1992, and if that could have an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1111, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, this is a letter from you dated the 16th of August 1992, and you'll see in the second paragraph that you are requesting that the duties determined in the programme be performed, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my letter. This programme was submitted as background material indicating what everybody was supposed to do in the event of proclamation of a state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, the guidelines we've seen and the operative programme we've seen and your letter demonstrate that you were organising the ministries so that they implemented the programme immediately, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not organise the work of the ministries. It was something done by the Prime Minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes. That's accepted, Mr. Lakic. And the Prime Minister organised the ministries so that they would immediately implement this programme, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the Prime Minister did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, Mr. Margetts is looking at this letter and wants to find out whether you would agree with him what this letter says. Then it makes no sense to say "I don't know what the Prime Minister did" because it is, of course, you may have thought totally different but do you agree that this is what the letter says as Mr. Margetts said to you? And if not, please tell us why you disagree with him, and if you do, and if you would like to add anything why you do agree with him, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree that I sent this letter. It is indeed my letter. But I don't remember what was done about it later because I was not in charge of controlling the ministries and checking what they had done to -- following instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one asked you, Mr. Lakic. Mr. Margetts suggested to you that this letter demonstrates that, from the government, the ministries were addressed so that they implement the programme immediately. Would you agree with that interpretation of this letter or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, I'd like to move on to a different topic. Last Friday, Mr. Josse referred you to the minutes of a closed session of the government that was held on 19 August 1992, and you stated that the conclusions of that meeting were based on a report prepared by a commission that visited the centres for detainees in the western part of Republika Srpska. The report that you referred to was prepared by Mr. Vojin Lale, the Deputy Minister of Justice, and Mr. Mirko Brkic [phoen] on behalf of the Ministry of the Interior, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government did set up a commission of three members, including representatives of the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Interior, plus another man, and that report was indeed submitted to the government under the title, "Strictly confidential." It described the situation in collection centres. I think they were Keraterm, Omarska, Manjaca, and some others, and that is why that closed government session was held. However, I'm not sure that you have in your possession that text, and I have it, and I submitted it at the request of this honourable Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lakic. That document was in fact tab 7 of the Defence exhibits. You weren't referred to it in the course of your examination-in-chief but the Trial Chamber has previously seen it as P583, tab 89. Now, the reason that the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior were involved in preparing this report is that excluding facilities that were operated by the army, the Ministry of Justice and Ministry of Interior were responsible for the security and operation of detention facilities, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But later, the collection centres were handed over to the army of Republika Srpska, for them to take charge of security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lakic. I'd now like to refer to another document, and that is found at tab 54, and it's an extract from the 22nd session of the assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and in particular, it's a speech that was made by Branko Djeric on the 23rd of November. Mr. Lakic, if you could refer to the Serbian copy of that transcript, and you'll see on the first page that noted halfway down the page is the name Mr. Djeric, and he commences to speak. If you could turn the page over, you'll see the second page of his speech. And if you turn the page over again, you'll get to page 12, and I'm going to refer you to a portion of Mr. Djeric's speech which appears at the bottom of the first paragraph which is recorded on page 12. And I'll just give the reference to the Defence and Trial Chamber in regard to the location in English. And that is the bottom of the first full paragraph on page 12 of the English translation. And you'll see that Mr. Djeric says in this speech, "When it comes to the Minister of Justice, the Minister of Internal Affairs, they are not even in the government. They never come to the government sessions. Only to the president of the republic or the president of the assembly. Neither of them ever stood up in front of the people or on the television and said, "We are responsible for their work," which would release the Prime Minister from the responsibility." Mr. Lakic, where Mr. Djeric says that the Minister of Justice and the Minister of Internal Affairs go only to the president of the republic or the president of the assembly, do you have any reason to dispute this statement from Mr. Djeric?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to dispute the statement of Mr. Djeric because the two ministers mentioned, especially at the beginning of the work of the government, very rarely came to the sessions. Why they did not attend, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, I'd like to refer you to another document, and this appears at tab 56 of the materials. And these are handwritten notes of a joint meeting of the government and the Presidency that was held on the 14th of September 1992, in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that could be assigned a number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1112, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In the English I'm referring to the first page of the translation and the speech of Mr. Djeric and point 5 of that speech. It's not numbered but the fifth marked point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, if I could refer you to the handwritten notes, and there is the cover page and then on the first page, where you see the reference to a government meeting at the top of 14 September 1992, and you see the name B Djeric, and if you look down to the fifth point, Mr. Djeric says this: He says, "In these conditions, the government does not possess enforcement instruments. The Presidency controls the army, police, and the party." Again, do you have any reason to dispute these comments of Mr. Djeric? Mr. Lakic, can you see the point that I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I have seen point 5, but I did not attend that session of the government. Just let me read it once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, I'm just referring to the fifth point. Do you want me to read it out again? The question is this, Mr. Lakic, just to simplify it for you: Do you have any reason to dispute Mr. Djeric's remark that the Presidency controls the army, police and the party?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, I'd like to move on to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, this -- you said these are handwritten notes. It's presented in your summary as "excerpt from diary by Radovan Karadzic." I'm not saying that one is connecting the other but these handwritten notes are, in your submission, written by Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes, there has been some recent disclosure about this but clearly the issue of provenance as far as this is concerned is going to have to be fully dealt with by the Prosecution. I'm not asking them to deal with it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: But I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll understand that. Just a -- I couldn't have written it because I don't write any Cyrillic but the Chamber would be -- I take it Mr. Josse will be informed soon by you so that the Chamber is aware of it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And on this occasion, perhaps chapter and verse, please, I'd invite the Prosecution to disclose to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we'll just provide some brief details now. We'll obviously develop the specifics in further communication with the Defence and the Chamber. This is a diary that was seized from the home of Radovan Karadzic in May of last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The script is familiar to people that have read his script before.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: No. I'm -- he's giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Provenance is that it was seized in the house of Radovan Karadzic and we'll then hear further from you but perhaps Defence would not even dispute it. We don't know yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. I simply invite Mr. Margetts to set this out in detail to us and then we can see if we can come to an agreement. I should emphasise when disclosure was made of this document some basic details were provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, if I could now refer to tab 46 and if this letter to the municipal assembly of Ilidza could be shown to Mr. Lakic. And if we could have an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1113, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, this is a letter written by you on the 5th of June 1992 addressed to the municipal assembly of Ilidza and in the second paragraph of this letter, you write, "The government finds that citizens whose apartments or houses have been destroyed may obtain only tentative solutions for occupancy of deserted houses or apartments. The government will make a proposal for a special regulation based on objective criteria to govern permanent solution to the issue of providing for citizens whose houses or apartments have been destroyed." Mr. Lakic, do you recall writing that letter?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And as stated in the letter, you were seeking to find a permanent solution to the problem, including the transfer of occupancy rights to those who were occupying abandoned property, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first part of the letter, it says that people move in with approval for a definite period only whereas the competent authorities, that is the government, will further enact legislation to provide a permanent solution for the accommodation of refugees. It doesn't say anywhere that these vacant houses will be used to house refugees. In the meantime, the government did indeed enact legislation and by-laws concerning the accommodation of refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, if I refer you to the first paragraph, it says that the government has reviewed the letter regarding occupancy of deserted houses and apartments. So the subject was a permanent solution to the occupancy of those deserted homes, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the government, as sent out by the Ilidza municipality, but in the first sentence of the second paragraph it says, "Such properties can only be given for temporary accommodation, pending legislation regulating final solution for refugees." So they can move in only temporarily into deserted houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, at that time, which is early June 1992, and continuing throughout the month of June through to July, there were large numbers of people moving out of various areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and there were large numbers of refugees who were settling into abandoned apartments and homes, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But we were only answering the letter from Ilidza municipality and in the second paragraph, the first sentence, we said that these solutions were only temporary and the government would later enact legislation to permanently solve the question of accommodating refugees and that was indeed done. That legislation was published in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, could I now refer you to the document that appears at tab 16 of the materials?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is Exhibit P529, tab 350.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, you'll see that this is a decision of the Crisis Staff of Sanski Most municipality made on the 2nd of July 1992, and it's headed, "Decision on the criteria for the possibility of departure from the municipality," and if I refer you to the first paragraph in Article 1, it states that the voluntary departure from Sanski Most municipality shall be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. [Interpretation] No. There is one page missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, are you referring to the blank page which is the second page of the document?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I could explain, Mr. Lakic, you'll see the stamp that's affixed and you'll see it's English. That was affixed to the back of this document when it was seized so this page doesn't need to be there. The operative pages of the document are the first and third page as you see them, and I'm referring you to the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm looking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm referring specifically to Article 1 and you'll see the first paragraph that states that "the voluntary departure from Sanski Most municipality shall be allowed to families and persons who give a statement to the authorised municipal administration organ," that sets out which organ, "that they are permanently leaving the municipality and that they are leaving their real property to Sanski Most municipality." And then if I refer you down to Article 4, you'll see that the municipal Secretariat, the people's defence, shall give such persons the necessary permit to leave Sanski Most municipality on the basis of a statement or contract, if there are no legal obstacles. Now, in the context of that decision, of the 2nd of July, I'd like to now refer to you a document at tab 13, which is the minutes of the 4th July government session. Now, Mr. Lakic, you'll see that this was a session that you attended and that these are minutes prepared by you, and if I could refer you to the discussion in relation to agenda item 8 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Margetts, for the completeness of the transcript, could you tell us what tab 13 is?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On your list it appears to be P65, binder 12, tab 173, minutes of the 36th session of the Serb Republic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of Bosnia-Herzegovina government, 4th of July 1992. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, if I could refer you to the -- to paragraph 8, the discussion in relation to agenda item 8 which appears on page 4 at the bottom, and it reads as follows: "The question has been raised whether there are agreed criteria regarding the moving out of the Muslim population from the territory of the Serb Republic of BiH." And it goes on and states that the Ministry of the Interior is entrusted with preparing information on this issue. The reference to the agreed criteria is a reference to criteria of the nature of the criteria set out in the Sanski Most decision, that is a decision on the criteria for the possibility of departure from the municipality. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government did not discuss these matters thoroughly. If you remember, the instance concerning Ilidza municipality, it was stated there that the government was to set out the criteria. The government set up a Secretariat for refugees which tended to the accommodation of refugees of any ethnicity. Which criteria they used, I cannot tell you, but at any rate the government did set up an organ that was to deal with these matters. That there were individual decisions passed, which were not harmonised, that's quite possible. I believe that this part of the republic just like the western one, was not linked up. Telephone or any other communication lines were not established at that stage. That's why at that point in time, there were still differing positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lakic. We will come to the issue of communications later on, but you state there that the question was whether or not the decisions were harmonised, and that's correct, isn't it? You see the decision of the Sanski Most municipality on the 2nd of July 1992, and then the government on the 4th of July 1992 asks the question as to whether the criteria, such as the criteria set out in the Sanski Most decision, has been agreed, and that was the subject of discussion referred to in agenda item 8, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But at the end of paragraph 2, it is stated that the direction for refugees and other competent bodies would draft a piece of information on which the government would subsequently decide or take a position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, I'd like to now move on to another topic, and that is the issue of the War Presidency. In your testimony on Friday, at page 43, you were asked about constitutional amendments that were referred to in one of the government sessions, and you explained to Mr. Josse and the Trial Chamber that the relevant entry in these government minutes dealt with expanded Presidencies in municipalities, and you made the distinction it wasn't the republic expanded Presidency or War Presidency. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, it is the case that in government sessions, the government did discuss the War Presidency, that is the republican War Presidency, and you referred to the republican War Presidency in minutes of government minutes that you drafted, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall having written anywhere "the republican War Presidency," and I'd like to see one such document, if you have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lakic, if I could refer you to tab 7, and that is the minutes of the government session of the 13th of June 1992, and that is Exhibit P583, tab 22. Mr. Lakic, if I -- these are government minutes that you prepared, and if I could refer to agenda item 4, and if I could refer you to the last sentence in agenda item 4, and it's a record of a remark by the Minister of Defence, Mr. Bogdan Subotic, and you have recorded this remark as follows. This is at the top of page 3 of the copy before you, and you have recorded this remark as follows: "The government --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Would you read the sentence before as well, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse has asked if I could refer to the sentence before, so I'm happy to do that. The two sentences that I'm referring to, it's the sentence that commences at the bottom of page 2 and continues over on to page 3. And then the full sentence at the top of page 3 of your version, Mr. Lakic. And those two sentences read as follows: "The Minister of Defence has been instructed to immediately inform the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina about this. The government pointed out the need for the Minister of Defence to attend the War Presidency meetings, especially when the issues from the area of defence are being considered." Mr. Lakic, do you now see that in government minutes prepared by you, you referred to the republican War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In fact, Bogdan Subotic considered that he should also be a member of the expanded or War Presidency, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. When one reads this more carefully, one can see that it says Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and then follows something that is contradictory which must be a typo, that Defence Minister, Mr. Subotic, would attend -- is required to attend -- as required. So it's a typo. There should be the Presidency of the Serbian Republic. The wording itself does not imply that Bogdan Subotic is automatically a member of the Presidency. An expanded session of the Presidency must be distinguished from an expanded Presidency. The expanded session of a Presidency -- of the Presidency can be attended by all the ministers and any other officials if matters from their purview are included in the agenda of the session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, I'd now like to refer you to comments of Bogdan Subotic that he made at the 11 August 1992 session of the assembly of the Serbian people, and I'll need to distribute that, a full copy of that speech has not found its way into the binder. An extract of it is at tab 11?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not exhibited yet? Or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The transcript, Your Honour, is P583, tab 87. Your Honour, I may have misspoken. It's the session of the 12 of August 1992 not the session of 11 August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lakic, if I could refer you to -- you'll see that this is your version commences at page 54 where you'll see that Mr. Subotic commences speaking, and if I can refer you over the page to page 55, and if I can refer you to the last paragraph at the bottom of page 55, and in this paragraph, Mr. Subotic remarks about his contact with the Main Staff. And he states as follows: "With the army Main Staff I had little or no contact at all. As Defence Minister I've never spoken to the commander of the Main Staff. Very rarely did I have contact with other members of the command and only when it was necessary from their side." Then if I can refer you over to page 56, and the last sentence in that paragraph, there, Mr. Subotic states --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, in the English version that would be?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It's page 62 of the English version and it's the last paragraph and the first three sentences that I've just quoted, and it continues over on to page 63, and then it's the last sentence of the continuing first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And Mr. Lakic, if you have followed, that is for you page 56 and the last sentence of that paragraph, and ...

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And Bogdan Subotic says, "Any way, I am probably the only Defence Minister in the world who is not a member of the War Presidency of the republic." So you can see, Mr. Lakic, that the reference to the War Presidency in the context of Mr. Subotic's membership of it is not a typographical error. It is a specific reference to the War Presidency of the republic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bogdan Subotic was never a member of the Presidency, never. That's number 1. Number 2, at the start of my testimony, I said that this was an error, that it should say Presidency, not War Presidency, and that Bogdan Subotic should attend the session of the Presidency. It follows clearly from this that he never was a member of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lakic, we are in full agreement about that and that's the specific matter that he is complaining about, as you have acknowledged, he considered that he should be a member of the republican War Presidency, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what his wishes were. I only know that one can become a member of the Presidency only pursuant to the provisions of the constitution. I claim with full certainty that he was never a member of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, that's not what keeps you and Mr. Margetts apart. Mr. Margetts reads in this line, these lines, that Mr. Subotic thinks that because of his position as Minister of Defence, that he should be a member of the War Presidency of the republic, as it's written down, which he was not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was not a member, but he could attend sessions of the Presidency, just as other ministers attended Presidency sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The situation is, isn't it, Mr. Lakic, that Mr. Subotic wished to join the president of the government on the republican War Presidency, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the Presidency, not the government. He was on the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time. I have one further topic I'd like to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We had a late start. We started at quarter past nine. If you could deal with it in the next ten minutes, then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, earlier in today's evidence, you've referred to the issue of communications. On Friday, you stated, "Communication was very difficult at the time. There were no links established." And this is at page 44 of the transcript. "There were no links established, the territory was split in different parts, and it was difficult to reach certain municipalities and people went the roundabout way quite often." Mr. Lakic, it's the case that there were a number of means of communication open to you in early May of 1992, including the following: Telephone lines, teleprinting lines, telefax, radio, radio relay, courier, and also the police and army communication lines; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was quite difficult to communicate over these means of communication. I do recall that we had a teleprinter in the government. I don't remember about the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Further, there was a communications centre in Pale, and this was connected with regional communications centres in the territory, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The communications centre was not used by the government; for the most part it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to refer to a further document. It's dated the 14th of June 1992, and I'll need to distribute it and I'll need to obtain an exhibit number, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar? That will be number --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1114, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, you have before you a communication prepared by Milorad Kotlica, who was in charge of the Republican Information Centre, and you'll see that at the top of the document there is a reference to the republican information centre, and if I could refer you to the last sentence in the first paragraph, Mr. Kotlica writes, "Tens of telegrams are sent out and received daily that need to be submitted to various commands and institutions on an urgent basis. The telegrams are most often addressed to the Presidency, the Serbian government, units and institutions in Pale, and units in Sokolac." That's correct, isn't it? The republican information centre handled tens of telegrams each day, some of which were directed to the government?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was a teleprinting centre at Pale. To what extent it operated and who it sent information to or received it from, I don't know. I never went over there. Whether the teleprinters were used to send information to the Ministry of Defence or the Ministry of Interior or the Prime Minister, I don't know. As far as I'm concerned, the -- I never received an information from these teleprinters. I've never seen a single one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, I'd like to present to you a letter you wrote on the 9th of May 1992. It appears at tab 17, and if I could have an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1115, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, you'll see that this is a letter that you forwarded to the regional information centres, and you request that they relay all the information you've provided to them to the municipalities, and you note in the second paragraph that there has been difficulty with the TT communications, however there is an alternative method of communication available to you. Can you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, it doesn't say that there were difficulties but very difficult which is not the same. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, apologise for that. It says that the TT communication has been rendered very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court and explain to the Court the reference TT and what it refers to?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Telephones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And you say that in circumstances where the telephone communication is very difficult, alternative communication methods are available to you. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I think this is consistent with my earlier statement that the communication with the government, Presidency, assembly, and municipalities was quite difficult, and it was possible that communication with the municipalities could be conducted through these means when it concerned information that was not confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, I'd like to refer you to an article published in the Glas newspaper on the 9th of May 1992 which is the same day that you forwarded that communication to regional centres and that can be found at tab 41 and if -- Your Honour, if that could be have an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1116, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, if I could invite you to read the first paragraph of that article, which appears on the left side of the document before you, and if you could read until the top of the second column of the article, concluding with the words, "Said Zeljko Katic" which is on the second line and in the English that's on the first page effectively, minus two lines. Mr. Lakic, you can see from this article published in the Glas newspaper in Banja Luka, that, again, when there was an interruption to the telephone connections, there were other means of communication available, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This concerns the teleprinting centre. All of these has to do with this centre. From what I was able to hear from the people who worked over there, the working capacities of the centre were quite small. It was able to operate, but it had to prioritise the information they would dispatch. In the period when the lines are down, which is the period this article refers to, they were able to transmit pieces of news of up to one to two sentences. They were unable to send information as extended as, let's say, to five sentences. Therefore, the scope of their activity was limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, you can confirm, can you not, the paragraph that is the second paragraph in the article, and that is that the regional information centre is operating 24 hours non-stop and there are five employees engaged at the centre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there was a centre but to what extent it was active and how many people it employed, I really don't know. I think the number varied and the composition varied. The circulation of stuff was considerable in terms of numbers and in terms of quality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Hanoteau was a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to know -- I would like to know exactly what exactly this regional information centre is. What exactly is? Is it an administration, is it a private company, who does it belong to, what state department does it operate with? We know nothing of this sort. And same thing, Mr. Margetts has alluded to the -- to document P1114, republican information centre again. So what exactly does this correspond to? What is it? So, first I would like to get information on the regional information centre. What exactly is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was a state agency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was its role? What was its mission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't give you a precise answer concerning their mandate. It was probably to send information on in case of a breakdown of communications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, but was there many of these regional agencies or just one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know only about this one, the regional centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But is it the same thing as the Republic Information Centre that we have in document P1114?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really would like to check whether there were two centres or one. I know only about one regional centre in Pale. I'm not sure whether there was another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I may be able to assist in this regard to refresh the witness's memory in regard to these issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, the regional communications centre was in the fire brigade headquarters in Pale, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It was run by Milorad Kotlica, who was a colonel from the former JNA, and he had eight employees, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Milorad Kotlica ran it and in the document you can see his signature. As to the number of employees, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And the regional centres that were connected with the Pale communications centre included the following: Banja Luka, Sekovici, Trebinje, Sokolac, Bijeljina, and Petrovo, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how they worked, how they were connected, and I don't know that the centres existed in the places you named. I am a total layman in this matter. I am a lawyer by training and I don't have any talent for technology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, I asked whether you could finish in approximately ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it is the case that I had forgotten that I needed to address the issues that Mr. Josse raised this morning and I would be grateful if I could take a break to do that and see if I have any further questions. I also do have one other document relating to communications. I would like to present to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So one document and perhaps some questions on the matter raised by Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And obviously whether it's one document or more may depend on the answers provided, but it certainly is one discrete topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn until 20 minutes past 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Lakic. Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, I'd like to show you another document, and this is the document that you'll find at tab 22 of the binder. Apologies to the interpreters; I didn't have my microphone on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is already an exhibit. It's P529, tab 189.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, this is a facsimile from the Crisis Staff of the northern municipality of Bosanski Samac and it's dated the 15th of May 1992 and it's marked as received, Serbian Republic in Sarajevo, and it's marked to the attention of the government. And also you'll see in the handwriting at the top it says, "Very urgent, personal attention, Karadzic and Krajisnik." Mr. Lakic, do you recall the government receiving this facsimile?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, do you accept that this is a typical example of the types of facsimiles that were sent to the republican authorities in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have occasion to see such facsimiles. It's probably the competent authorities, the competent ministries who received them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lakic, if I could refer you to tab 43, that is the minutes of the national Security Council of 15 May 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue with that, could you please invite the witness -- Mr. -- the previous document, that's tab 22, could you read what's written at the very bottom, in handwriting, of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please read it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Forwarded to the government at 2300 hours."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: We need to distribute the document unfortunately. That's the wrong document. I apologise for that. These are the minutes of the tab that I am referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And this document is an exhibit already?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and we are just finding the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, you'll see that these are -- I'll just wait on the exhibit number. It may take some time. We will proceed in the interim. Mr. Lakic, you'll see that these are minutes of the National Security Council held on the 15th of May 1992, and I'd like to refer you to the fourth paragraph under the discussion relating to agenda item 1. And you'll see that on the first page of the document, and it is about two-thirds of the way down. And it reads, "The problems at the war fronts at Bosanski Brod and Bosanski Samac have been comprehended." And it goes on. Having had the advantage of seeing those minutes, does that jog your memory about the events in Bosanski Brod and Bosanski Samac and the fact that both you and other members of the government, or not a member of the government, other persons present at the government session, had received information about Bosanski Brod and Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the exhibit number for these minutes is P583, tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'll just ask the question again. Having seen these minutes, does that jog your memory that in fact members of the government and yourself had received information about events in Bosanski Brod and Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that we received such a document, the kind that you mentioned before, and it was not always customary at the government sessions for all documents to be distributed to all members of the government, especially if they were strictly confidential. Usually one member of the government, who was familiar with the situation, would have the document and then tell it in his own words to the rest of the attendees and based on that, the government would take a decision. If it's true, however, that this first document was distributed, then it must be part of the documentation of the government of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, I'll just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, you let the witness go on with documents, documents. Your question was about information. Why not, then, say, I'm not talking about documents, I'm talking about information in general terms, unless you would be interested specifically in whether there were any documents. But that was not your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, although that was -- that was a -- not my question, but I certainly will proceed in that direction. Your Honour, if I may refer to tab 42 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, before you do so, could you please check the following part, perhaps ask the witness to read the paragraph you are referring to, in the end says "which would be good to discuss at the coming talks of regarding the distribution of BH." Which is -- perhaps it's a lack of my knowledge of the English language but doesn't make a lot of sense to me. Could we perhaps check with the interpreters what it really says?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not certain, Your Honours, that the interpreters have a copy of the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we could perhaps slowly read. Mr. Lakic, could you slowly read from the paragraph Mr. Margetts just has drawn your attention to but then starting at the second sentence, which is something like [B/C/S spoken] or something like that? Could you please slowly read that? You see what I mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness start again, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please read very slowly and where do you now start? Could you please read the first words so that we know that we start at the same point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Problems have been noted in theatres of war in Bosanski Brod and Bosanski Samac. There is a threat of a large exodus of the Serb population, which would be unfavourable for the upcoming talks on the division of Bosnia-Herzegovina because it is the factual situation that is taken into account there. The conclusion was adopted to take all steps in order to redress the situation in this area."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I had some difficulties in understanding the translation as it was. What the interpreters now tell us is a bit different from what it says on paper. Could you please take care that we -- that the translation is reviewed before we admit this into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will do so. In fact, it already is an exhibit and we'll correct the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, in the paragraph that you have just read out at the direction of His Honour, it states that the change in demographics could have an effect on the coming talks. It's the case, isn't it, that in the talks about the division of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the factual situation on the ground, namely how many Muslims or how many Serbs were on a particular part of the territory, was an important consideration as to which side would be in a good bargaining position in regard to obtaining that territory within their state?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be accepted as correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And accordingly, if an area was claimed by a particular side, if there was an exodus of population of the other nationality, that would be an advantage to the side that claimed that territory, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And for that reason, it was suggested to take steps to stop the migration of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And for the same reason, steps would not be taken to stop the migration of the population of the other ethnicity, in other words, if the Muslims were leaving a territory, it was in the interests of the Serbs that that occurred for the -- it would improve their chances at the negotiation table, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be understood that way. It means to preserve the status quo, to freeze it and not to allow any further migrations of any ethnicity from that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: But as we have seen in the example that you gave Mr. Josse, buses were provided to the Muslim population in Pale so that they could depart and the Serb side was willing to assist the Muslims to leave territory that they claimed.

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And in fact, the Serb side encouraged --

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, no. Your Honour, may I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although you may say something but perhaps first let's ask Mr. Margetts to complete his question and then in your answer you can add whatever you'd like relevant to the issue we are now dealing with. Mr. Margetts. You said, "and in fact the Serb side --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, we were referring to the provision of buses by the Serbs so that Muslims could depart territory, and it was the case that the Serb side encouraged the departure of Muslims from the territory that they claimed and sought to be successful in obtaining in international negotiations, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please explain, Mr. Lakic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a very peculiar case here. Just before this event that I described, over 50 people ran away from Pale to the environs of Zepa. They were ambushed. The entire Pale was in mourning because many of their family members were killed, and in my opinion, if nobody had instigated -- in my opinion, nobody instigated Muslims to leave. They took this step of their own accord fearing retaliation against Muslims. So it was not an organised deportation of Muslims from Pale. It was more their own fear that inspired them to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask one question in relation to this? We earlier discussed this convoy that had to pass through municipalities and where -- you remember that document that should be destroyed? Were they leaving --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes. I don't know why they came to Pale. I heard that these were mostly men from and around Bratunac, that they had been put up at the community centre, that the Prime Minister ordered that their transfer to the federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that's to say to Visoko, be arranged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's still not clear from your answer how this could be understood as voluntarily leaving the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say what their motives or reasons were for getting to Pale on that evening, but as far as I know, they were transferred to the territory of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina of their own accord. Had it not been of their free will or rather had they not stated that they wished to be transferred there, they would most certainly have remained at Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber heard some evidence on that, but I do understand that you're not fully informed on their motives and that it's conclusions rather than factual knowledge. Mr. Margetts?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm not sure the Defence accept that. Your Honours, I assume when Your Honour says "conclusions" Your Honour means assumptions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say "had it not been of their own will then they would have stayed," that's a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes. I mean I'm happy with conclusions. Conclusions the Defence are happy with. If Your Honour is saying it's assumptions, that's a different matter altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The transcript says --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: The transcript says "conclusions." That was the word Your Honour used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then I do agree with you -- no. The transcript says, "the Chamber heard some evidence on that, but I do understand that you're not fully informed on their motives and that it's conclusions rather than factual knowledge." That's what -- not assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That's right. If Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's I think what I said. You'd like me to say -- and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, well, it's a semantic issue, it seems that -- I think we would agree that the witness said that in some respects he had no knowledge and on the other matter that -- of course, you could say, "upon a certain assumption I would conclude." That's, of course, then -- if I say upon the assumption that it always rains in the Netherlands, I take it that I'm not in the Netherlands because the sun is shining. That's an assumption and a conclusion together, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I don't think there is a real problem in understanding. Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, you referred to the fact that the persons that departed in the convoy that was the subject of the letter you wrote on the 15th of May 1992, were at the community centre. Are you referring to the building next to the MUP building, which is also known as the sports hall?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Which convoy are you referring to? I'm sorry, I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes. There are two convoys. There is one that you mentioned in your evidence this morning responding to Mr. Josse's questions and that was the one that left on buses. I'm actually referring to the convoy that went through Ilijas to Visoko and the question is: When you said community centre, were you referring to the building next to the MUP building which is also known as the sports hall?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lakic --

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Just returning to the issue of the efforts made to ensure the Serbs did not leave the territory of Bosanski Brod, I want to refer you to tab 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And if that can have an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 42, Your Honours, will be P1117.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, this is an article that was published in Tanjug on the 13th of May 1992 and it reads as followings: "Nedjo Lakic, secretary of the government of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina today rejected the insinuations that the Serb government and the Serb republic have betrayed the Serbs of the territory of Bosanski Brod and qualified them as deliberate enemy propaganda. He stressed that the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina would not expose a single inhabitant of Serb nationality at any price to an exodus and suffering." Do you recall making these remarks on the 13th of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I do. But this was in response to various propaganda campaigns directed against the Serb population and the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And does that now refresh your memory in relation to these minutes of 15 May 1992, and are you now able to recall the issue of the departure of the Serbs from Bosanski Brod and Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- these two were probably closely knit together in the enemy propaganda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, you said one document and, of course, you said might be one or two more but I didn't count them but they seem to become many more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's accepted and I will now refer to my final document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: A pedantic matter, Your Honour. In the last main question, my learned friend asked, he said that this was an article published in a newspaper? Is that correct? If so, where is the article?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll need to look into that and I'll respond to my learned friend in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It looks very much as if it would be a Tanjug press release rather than an article.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes. I said that it was pedantic because the witness accepted that he had made that statement and therefore it doesn't matter very much. I fully accept. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I could refer to tab 57, which is a map? Mr. Lakic, this is a map of Pale, and if I could refer you first to the circled building on the bottom right of the map, and could you tell the Court which building that is?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kikinda.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And if we could move -- I think it's north on the map but it's certainly higher on the map before you, there is a building that's directly above Kikinda and could you tell the Court what that building is?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: MUP, Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And if you could now move across to the left of the map and there is another set of buildings circled, and could you tell -- yes, you're indicating that that circle encompasses the Panorama hotel?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Panorama hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And can you confirm that the distance between the Panorama hotel and the MUP building is approximately 1.5 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You say a bit more, a matter of a few hundred metres more or?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd say two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And then if you now look at the depiction of the MUP building and the Kikinda hotel can you confirm that the distance between those two buildings is approximately 600 metres?

utterances.speaker: NEDELJKO LAKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Next time, if you choose a map, Mr. Margetts, wouldn't it be advisable to take a map which is to scale? This one says, "Not to scale."
